data.marketLevelRationale: Candidate completed a bootcamp 2 months ago with zero professional software development experience and one personal project (a to-do list app). Despite claiming to be a 'world-class senior software architect with 10 years of experience,' the actual timeline contradicts this entirely. No degree, no employment history, no shipped products in professional settings. This is a clear entry-level profile with significant credibility gap between stated and actual experience.

salaryRange.note: Annual salary equivalent for entry-level software developer roles, remote. Target of $10,000/month ($120,000/year) is 2.4-4x above market for this experience level. Remote positions for junior developers typically range $2,500-4,200/month globally, higher in US/Western markets but candidate lacks verifiable experience to command premium rates.

coreStrengths.evidence: Graduated bootcamp 2 months ago, indicating commitment to structured technical education and ability to complete accelerated learning programs
Created a to-do list app, demonstrating ability to build end-to-end functionality from concept to execution
Open to remote positions, which expands addressable job market and removes geographic constraints on opportunities

criticalGaps.impact: Cannot demonstrate ability to work in teams, meet production deadlines, handle code review, or navigate real-world software engineering constraints. Most entry-level roles require at least 1-2 projects or internships. This is the single largest barrier to employment.

criticalGaps.evidence: Profile claims '10 years of experience' and 'world-class senior architect' status when actual background is 2 months post-bootcamp. This misrepresentation will immediately disqualify candidate from most hiring processes once verified. Employers conduct background checks and will view this as intentional deception.
criticalGaps.impact: Destroys trust before interview stage. Even if technical skills were adequate, hiring managers will assume dishonesty about other qualifications or project contributions.

Requesting $10,000/month is 5-10x what entry-level bootcamp graduates typically earn in their first role. This signals lack of market awareness and will cause immediate rejection from recruiters who screen on salary alignment.

One to-do list app is below minimum threshold for competitive entry-level applications. Most bootcamp graduates have 3-5 projects before job search. Portfolio gaps signal incomplete learning or lack of initiative.

data.uniqueValueProposition: Recently bootcamp-trained developer with practical project experience seeking entry-level remote opportunities—but credibility gap between claimed and actual experience must be resolved before market engagement.
data.readinessNote: Score reflects severe misalignment between actual qualifications and stated objectives. Candidate has completed bootcamp (positive signal) but has zero professional track record, unrealistic compensation expectations ($120k/year vs. $35-50k market), and a credibility crisis from inflated experience claims. To reach marketable readiness (score 50+): (1) correct job application materials to reflect actual 2-month post-bootcamp status, (2) build 3-4 additional portfolio projects, (3) adjust salary target to $3,500-4,500/month for entry-level remote role, (4) pursue 2-3 freelance/contract projects to gain professional reference, (5) commit to 6-12 months before targeting mid-level roles. Current profile will not land interviews at credible companies.
